Thank you, Mr. Chair. The subject property is addressed as 157 Schweitzer Street and is located
at the intersection of Lark and Schweitzer Streets in the Bridgeport East planning community.
The immediately surrounding areas comprise primarily of low-rise residential land uses.
The Croatian Roman Catholic Church owns the vacant lands directly across the street.
Croatian Church itself and the Kitchener border with Willits Township is located approximately 180 metres to the east.
Sylvia Park is located 360 metres to the southwest.
west. The subject property has 24.7 metres of frontage on Schweitzer Street and 50.9
metres of frontage on Lark Street and is approximately 1,400 square metres in area,
or about a third of an acre. The property is developed with a one-storey single detached
house that was constructed in the early 1960s. The subject property is identified as community
areas on map 2, urban structure of the Official Plan. The plan function of community areas
is to provide for residential land uses as well as non-residential supporting uses.
Limited intensification is permitted. The property is currently designated on
Map 3 land use shown on the screen as low-rise residential. This designation accommodates
a full range of low-density housing types which may include single detached dwellings,
semi-detached dwellings, additional dwelling units, townhouses, low-rise multiple dwellings,
and other types of low-rise housing. In this designation, no building is permitted to exceed
three storeys in height. The lands are currently zoned residential 3 or R3 in Zoning Bylaw 85.1.
That's the older Zoning Bylaw. This zoning permits single detached dwellings, additional dwelling
units, lodging houses, among other low-density housing forms. And the R3 zone outlines certain
requirements such as minimum lot area, quarter lot width, maximum building height and maximum
lot coverage. The applicant is requesting a zoning bylaw amendment to change the zoning
from R3 under the old zoning bylaw to Res4 under the new zoning bylaw which is 2019-051.
Along with a site-specific provision to facilitate the future creation of three new lots with frontage
on Lark Street, each to be developed with a new two-storey single-detached dwelling.
The site-specific provision would accomplish the following for the existing dwelling.
It would permit a minimum front yard setback of 4.2 metres to recognize the existing setback,
and it would permit a minimum rear yard setback of 5 metres to recognize an existing setback.
For the proposed dwellings, the site-specific provision would reduce the minimum rear yard
setback from 7.5 to 6.8 metres.
The existing dwelling near the intersection would be retained and the detached garage
would be demolished.
It should be noted that the existing single detached dwelling is presently occupied by
tenants and these tenants were advised of the subject proposal when they moved in.
The tenants are not required to relocate because the dwelling is not proposed to be demolished.
The tenants will continue to live in the existing house.
Each new single detached dwelling would have a lot width of 9 metres and a depth of 27.5
metres and would have a lot area of 246 square metres.
These lots are proposed to be created sometime after Council's decision regarding the subject
zoning bylaw amendment.
And a consent application would be required to actually create the lots at some point
in the future.
A conceptual rendering is shown on the screen, and this shows a single detached dwelling
that's two storeys in built form, and it has a single car garage.
Staff suggests that the proposed development represents an opportunity.
The proposal will facilitate gentle intensification of the lands with infill development in the
form of single detached dwellings.
It would further diversify the zone categories within this neighbourhood and consequently
the built form it would support and be supported by local transit and the nearby park.
It would assist in achieving the planned function of the city's urban structure.
It would allow for new development while retaining an existing dwelling and efficiently used
land infrastructure and services.
Staff responded to the questions and comments of the community at the virtual neighbourhood
meeting on June 26th.
Staff also responded to emails and voicemails.
The request in zoning by-law amendment represents good planning and staff supports the proposal.

I will begin by providing an overview of this one-time Zoning By-law Amendment application.
This application is submitted under Council Policy MUNPLA 1170.
This policy allows landowners to submit one-time Zoning By-law Amendment application at no
cost to facilitate a use change or to add a permitted use in a floodplain zone.
This is a streamlined Zoning By-law Amendment.
There was no public engagement except for a notification in the newspaper about this
public meeting in accordance with the council policy.
This application was circulated to applicable city department and external authorities for
comments.
Dan Merovitz has made an application for a zoning bylaw amendment for the subject property
addressed at 434-436 Queen Street South as shown in the screen.
The subject property is located in the Mill Courtland Woodside Park neighbourhood, south
of Courtland Avenue East and backs onto Schneider Creek.
It is surrounded by land designated as Existing Flood Plane Zone and Natural Conservation
Zones.
The site is entirely within the floodplain.
The site contains an existing two-storey building with a mix of views.
The ground floor is a personal service use and the second floor contains two dwelling
units.
The building functions as a semi-detached structure with adjoining half located in the
neighbouring property addressed 432 Queen Street South.
The purpose of the EUF zone is to recognise existing uses within floodways or floodplains.
The property is designated as Natural Heritage Conservation in the Official Plan.
The primary intent of the Natural Heritage Conservation land use is to protect and conserve
natural heritage features and its associated ecological functions.
The Official Plan policies considers an alternative uses in the EU F1 zone, if they are compatible
with the surrounding neighbourhood, if there is no new dwelling units proposed, if the use
proposes less risk in the floodplain, and if the Grand River Conservation Authority
has no concerns with it.
The applicant is requesting to allow the proposed retail use on the ground floor.
The Zoning By-law amendment is required to permit the additional new permitted use.
The amendment proposes to add a site-specific, in this case number 437, to Zoning By-law
There is no proposals for additions, alteration or replacements of existing buildings.
The maximum building floor area and setbacks set out in the Zoning By-law would not be
applied.
There is no other alternative zoning regulations that will be required to be added to the site-specific.
The proposed retail use is not expected to increase the flood-related risk to the property
nor its residents, tenants, or customers.
It's compatible with the neighbourhood and appropriate for the site.
The Grand River Conservation Authority has been directly involved in the review of this
application.
The Grand River Conservation Authority has confirmed that there is no objection to the
proposed use of the existing building and land, as it will not result in additional
impact to the flood flow or increase the flood risk.
As a conclusion, Development and Housing Approval staff are supportive of the proposed Zoning
By-law amendment application to permit the retail on the subject land.
